subject: biology
title: Prokaryotes vs Eukaryotes Adventure
welcome_lead: Today you'll compare prokaryotic and eukaryotic cells and tour the major organelles.
meta_desc: A-Level Biology Cells — prokaryotes vs eukaryotes, rough/smooth ER, Golgi, mitochondria, chloroplasts, lysosomes, and ribosome differences.
final_note: You learned that prokaryotes have 70S ribosomes and no nucleus, while eukaryotes have 80S ribosomes and membrane-bound organelles each with a specialised role.

concepts.def: Cell with no nucleus, 70S ribosomes, circular DNA — e.g. bacteria
Cell with nucleus and membrane-bound organelles, 80S ribosomes
Studded with ribosomes — synthesises and folds proteins
No ribosomes — synthesises lipids and steroids
Modifies, packages and labels proteins into vesicles
Vesicle of hydrolytic enzymes — breaks down waste

walkthroughs.body_html:
Prokaryotes are simpler and smaller (~1–5 µm).

Features:
- No nucleus — DNA is a single circular loop in cytoplasm
- 70S ribosomes (smaller)
- Cell wall of peptidoglycan (murein)
- Often have plasmids, pili, capsule, flagella

Eukaryotes are larger (~10–100 µm) with a true nucleus, 80S ribosomes, and membrane-bound organelles.

Proteins follow a production line:

1. Nucleus → mRNA leaves through nuclear pores
2. Rough ER → ribosomes translate mRNA; protein folded into ER lumen
3. Transport vesicle buds off
4. Golgi apparatus → modifies (e.g. adds sugars), packages
5. Secretory vesicle → fuses with plasma membrane (exocytosis)

Smooth ER handles lipids and steroid hormones instead.

Mitochondria — double membrane, inner folded into cristae, fluid matrix. Site of aerobic respiration → ATP.

Chloroplasts — double membrane, contain stacks of thylakoids (grana) in a fluid stroma. Site of photosynthesis.

Lysosomes — vesicles full of hydrolytic enzymes; digest worn-out organelles and engulfed pathogens.

Mitochondria and chloroplasts have their own DNA + 70S ribosomes (endosymbiotic theory).
